newsitem.title: USA: Palm Beach Cty, Fla. cogeneration bonds to default.
newsitem.headline: Palm Beach Cty, Fla. cogeneration bonds to default.

text.p: The owners of a Palm Beach County, Fla., cogeneration plant will not make the July 1 debt service payment on $128.5 million of bonds that financed the plant, putting the bonds in default, a spokesman for the owners said Monday.

Bondholders have been notified that the owners, who filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy reorganization in May, will not make the $4.6 million debt service payment on Tuesday, John Sullivan, a spokesman for the partnership, told Reuters.
The decision was made even though there is a debt service reserve fund adequate to cover the payment, he said.
"We feel it is in the best interest of the estate and all its creditors, which I would emphasize includes the bondholders, to retain these funds at this time," Sullivan said.

The industrial development bonds that will default are $120.5 million of Osceola Power Limited Partnership Project, tax-exempt series 1994 A, and $8 million of Osceola Power Limited Partnership Project, taxable Series 1994 B.
The owners would have had to obtain bankruptcy court permisson to make the payment, he said.

"We chose not to do that. That doesn't mean the payment won't be made at some point," Sullivan said. "Our judgment was that it's still very early in the bankruptcy process and therefore, its only prudent in our view that we protect our collateral at this stage. We're still assessing the process."
Sullivan said no decision had been made on whether the owners will make the Aug 15 debt service payment on a third series used to finance a second cogeneration plant.

If that $5.4 million payment is also missed, another $160 million of Palm Beach County industrial development bonds will default. That issue is Okeelanta Power Limited Partnership Project, Series 1993A.
All three series of bonds have been in technical default since the partnerships sought Chapter 11 protection in May, but no payment had previously been missed.
The plants are owned by the Okeelanta Power and Osceola Power Limited Partnerships. The partnerships are owned by affiliates of PG&E Corp, Bechtel Enterprises and Flo-Sun Inc.
Flo-Sun is one of Florida's largest sugarcane growers but has no liability toward the bonds, Sullivan said.
Nor does Palm Beach County have any liability toward the unrated bonds, a county official said.
Sullivan said the owners had worked closely with the bondholders and "we would certainly hope to maintain a dialogue with them."
The plants burn waste products from sugarcane processing. The Okeelanta plant has 70 megawatts of generating capacity and the Osceola plant 52 megawatts.

The partnerships filed for bankruptcy protection after the plants' only source of revenue, Florida Power & Light Co., terminated contracts to buy electricity from them. Florida Power & Light is a unit of FPL Group and has claimed that the plants have frequently shut down, in violation of the agreement.
